title: Breadth, length, height, depth (Ephesians 3:14–19)
hookLine: Paul kneels and prays they know the love that surpasses knowledge
tomorrow: One Lord, one faith, one baptism

lines: NICAEA: STAND TO PRAY ON SUNDAYS.
cards: The Council of Nicaea, in 325, asked Christians to stand for prayer on Sundays and through the days of Pentecost.
In scripture, kneeling comes with a plea more than once: Solomon kneels to dedicate the temple, and Jesus kneels in the garden.
So when Paul writes, in the middle of Ephesians, for this cause I bow my knees, the posture carries weight. He's on the floor. And what he asks for, down there, is not for himself.

teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ."

teach.h: ROOTED AND FOUNDED: A TREE, A HOUSE.
teach.b: He prays that they'll be strengthened in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in their hearts by faith, and then: "that being rooted and founded in charity, you may be able to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth."
Two pictures in one phrase. Rooted, like a tree. Founded, like a building.
And then four dimensions. Breadth, length, height, depth of what? Paul doesn't say.
He leaves the sentence open, as if the thing were too large to name. Readers have filled the space for centuries.
Saint Augustine saw the shape of the cross: the breadth of the crossbeam where the arms were stretched, the length of the upright, the height reaching up, the depth sunk in the ground.
Others hear simply the size of God's love in every direction.
Then Paul says what it all points to: "To know also the charity of Christ, which surpasseth all knowledge." To know what can't be known. It's a deliberate paradox.

teach.h: THE BREADTH, AND LENGTH, AND HEIGHT, AND DEPTH.
teach.b: In Paul's picture, this love can't be measured, and yet he prays they will come to know it, the way you know someone you love without being able to explain them.
Catholics still kneel at weighty moments: at the consecration during Mass, before the tabernacle, in confession. The posture says what Paul's says. This is too big to meet standing up.

how: Catholics kneel during parts of the Mass, including the consecration in the Eucharistic Prayer, before the Blessed Sacrament, and often at private prayer.

how far Paul traveled to plant churches

games.q: you're Paul, a prisoner, writing to the Ephesians. you kneel to pray. what do you ask for?
o: that they know Christ's love, rooted and founded in charity.
games.why: he prays that they comprehend the breadth, length, height and depth, and know "the charity of Christ, which surpasseth all knowledge."

practice: If your body allows, kneel on the floor or a cushion; if not, sit and bow your head low, and feel how different it is from standing: lower, smaller, steadier.

Picture something stretching out from you, wide, long, high and deep, without naming it yet. If you pray, pray for someone else, the way Paul did on his knees; if not, stay low and still, and let the room be large around you.

wordCard.voice: Breadth. The first of Paul's four dimensions: breadth, length, height and depth, the size of a love that surpasses knowledge. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: breadth, width. the first of four dimensions in Ephesians 3:18.

carryVoice: Your line: rooted in charity. Roots underneath, and love in every direction. Day five hundred eighty-four, in the books.
